mu_name_from: MuMain's ZzzOpenData.cpp loads the group as MODEL_SWORD + i from Sword{i+1}, so Sword08.bmd is index 7, which OpenMU's 0.75 table names the Falchion. MuWeapons.cs agrees from the client's side: `new("Falchion", "Sword08.bmd", WeaponStance.Sword, ...)`.
why_this_one: Hanzo's counter is the last shop in Lorencia with lines that do not resolve, and this is one of them. A shelf drops what it cannot draw - shared/Market builds the row and leaves out anything whose group and number find no asset - so the blacksmith sold ten of his twenty-four lines and the rest of the counter was empty air. Slot 73 at +3, and the line that actually stands there: it is written after the Gladius and overwrites it. A hundred and twenty strength, the second-highest gate on the counter.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: CreateWeapon(group, number, slot, skillNumber, width, height, dropsFromMonsters, name, dropLevel, minimumDamage, maximumDamage, attackSpeed, durability, magicPower, levelRequirement, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, energyRequirement, vitalityRequirement, wizardClass, knightClass, elfClass).
stats.width_note: Width is where OpenMU keeps two-handedness - `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` - and one here agrees with MuWeapons.cs's TwoHanded: false. It is also what takes a fifth off the price: shared/Market.Coin reads the footprint's width to tell a one-handed weapon from a two-handed one.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are the wizard, knight and elf flags, and MuWeapons.cs carries the same set from the client's side.
stats.skill_note: The skillNumber of the call. There are no skills in this simulation, so it is carried for the row to read against the call it came from and nothing more - and it is the reason this item is dearer in the original than the price MU2 charges, since OpenMU multiplies a skilled item's price by two and a half. See shared/Market's remarks.

stance_from: MuWeapons.cs: WeaponStance.Sword, TwoHanded: false. Actions 4 and 17, the family the Kris, the Short Sword and the Hand Axe already walk in. A one-handed blade leaves the shield hand free, which is the whole point of it on a counter that is mostly shields.
sheet_from: Data/Item/hound_sword1.OZJ (128x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names hound_sword1.jpg; 104 triangles, one mesh. The hound_ prefix is the same family the Plate and Big Round shields wear - MU groups a set of late 0.75 art under it rather than numbering it in sequence.
material_note:
Two islands on a hundred and four triangles, which is the coarsest split of anything in this batch: island 0 is ninety-four of them and covers the whole sword above the grip. It means (124, 119, 111) at chroma 13 - achromatic - and the sheet is a broad white blade with an engraved band along its spine and a dark ornate hilt at the end. Steel by majority.

Island 1 is the grip at (83, 74, 56) chroma 26. leather_wrap.
open_question: Island 0 is one material over a ground blade and a cast, pierced hilt - the same limit the Battle Axe's head island records, and a wider one, because here it is ninety-four triangles rather than a head. Splitting it would want the assignment to be finer than an island. The blade is most of the area, so the blade wins.
